name: Bellman-Ford Algorithm
description: Finds shortest paths from source to all vertices, even with negative edge weights. Detects negative cycles as a side effect. Slower than Dijkstra but more general.
aim: Find shortest distances from source by relaxing all edges V-1 times. After V-1 rounds any shorter path must have used a negative cycle.
howItWorks: Repeat V-1 times: relax every edge (u,v,w): if dist[u]+w < dist[v] then dist[v]=dist[u]+w
After V-1 iterations, check all edges again
If any edge still relaxes: NEGATIVE CYCLE detected

time.bestCase: Always performs V-1 passes over all E edges
time.averageCase: Same — no early termination possible in general

realWorld: Currency arbitrage detection (negative cycles = profit loop)
Financial risk analysis with negative payoffs
whenToUse: When Dijkstra cannot be used (negative weights)
alternatives: Dijkstra — O((V+E) log V) but only non-negative weights
Johnson's algorithm — reweights for all-pairs with negative edges
